case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed a permanent guardianship to non-relatives, holding that a court may reach the best-interests question only after finding the parent's rights terminated or suspended by circumstances under I.C. § 15-5-204, and that those circumstances had ceased once the mother appeared and objected.
key_cases.relevance: The controlling Idaho two-step for minor guardianships, and the parental presumption that must be overcome first.
key_cases.quote: "Suspended by circumstances" must contemplate some set of circumstances which deprives a parent of the ability to accept the rights and responsibilities of parenthood

key_cases.case_name: In re Adoption of John Doe
key_cases.holding: Affirming summary judgment for the Department, the court held that prospective adoptive parents cannot adopt a child in the Department's legal custody without the Department's written consent under I.C. § 16-1504(1)(f), and that the merits of their petition are immaterial absent that consent.
key_cases.relevance: Shows why families pursue guardianship: without Department consent, adoption is unavailable as a matter of law regardless of best interests.
key_cases.quote: The Department has the sole authority to withhold its permission from the prospective adoptive parents

key_cases.case_name: Idaho Department of Health & Welfare v. Doe
key_cases.holding: Affirming termination, the court held that the Department's reunification efforts and its placement choices are CPA requirements that are not relevant to whether the statutory grounds for termination are proved, and that the mother's due-process rights were protected by the clear-and-convincing burden at the termination trial.
key_cases.relevance: Recites the Department's permissible reasons for disfavoring a relative guardianship over adoption.
key_cases.quote: those cases also demonstrate that such findings are irrelevant to termination proceedings because reasonable efforts are requirements under the CPA, not Idaho's parental-rights termination statute

key_cases.case_name: Idaho Department of Health & Welfare v. Hays
key_cases.holding: Affirming the district court's reversal of the magistrate, the court held that where parental rights have been terminated and the Department is appointed guardian of the child's person, the Department alone must consent to an adoption and therefore alone selects the adoptive parents, subject only to the adoption court's power to deny a petition that is not in the children's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that the court may sanction a permanent placement other than adoption and must hold annual future-status hearings until one exists, which is the statutory space guardianship and long-term care occupy.
key_cases.quote: The authority to consent to the adoption of a child necessarily includes the authority to decide who can be the adoptive parents.
